messages.subject: How does the number of high-level parameters impact the cost of INLA ?
parts:
This question is completely unrelated with the one I just posted, but it is an interrogation I've had for a while and I think that the best answer is "from the horse's mouth". 

From the original paper of Rue, Martino, and Chopin, I understood that the collapsed maximum is found using quasi-Newton and then an exploration is done around the mode in order to determine credible intervals for the high level parameters and, correct me if I am wrong, compute credible intervals of the Gaussian effects of the model through various alternative procedures detailed in the paper. But if the space dimension goes higher, then the dimension of the high-density region around the node grows a lot. Also, I imagine that the quasi-Newton will suffer too. So, when does it start to hurt ? 

Thank you all again 
Sébastien
